messages.subject: qqplot for tweedie model
parts:
Hi,

Could anybody give me a hand in creating a qqplot for a tweedie model? I have spent a terrible amount of time with something that I feel somebody could do in minutes if not seconds.

Example code:

library(inlabru)
library(tweedie)

n <-100
x <- rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 0.2)
eta <- 1 + .5*x #- 7.1*x^2
mu <- exp(eta)
plot(x,mu)
p <- 1.1
phi <- 1.75
y <- numeric(n)
for(i in 1:n) {
  y[i] <- rtweedie(1, xi = p, mu = mu[i], phi = phi)
  }

r <- bru(y ~ 1 + f(x,model="linear"), data = data.frame(y, x),
          family = "tweedie")

Cheers,
iosu

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] qqplot for tweedie model
parts:
the documentation for tweeedie

inla.doc("tweedie")

shows how the parameterisation is compared to the one in the tweedie
package, and from that, you can just create your own qqplot, like for
the Gaussian

n=100
x=rnorm(n);
plot(sort(x), qnorm(1:n / (1+n)))

parts:
Thank you Havard for the response.

Yes, I found my way in the simple “just-intercept” sort of scenario. But when fitting a model I am having trouble to get the qnorm() part.

I looked into the mgcv package to see how they do it and I believe that I am stuck in the calculation of deviance residuals for this tweedie distribution. So, I lack the deviance.residuals() function in the code below. inlabru provides residuals in the output, but I am being incapable to replicate them by hand. I tried to dig in bru() to find where/how the residuals are computed but I havent been able to find it.


0 - data and model fit

library(inlabru)
library(tweedie)

p <- 1.1
phi <- 1.75
y <- numeric(n)
for(i in 1:n) {
  y[i] <- rtweedie(1, xi = p, mu = mu[i], phi = phi)
  }
r <- bru(y ~ 1 + f(x,model="linear"), data = data.frame(y, x),

family = "tweedie") 

1- simulate model residuals by generating new data based on the fitted model and calculate the residuals for that new data

for(j in 1:rep){
 sample_model=c()
  for(i in 1:n) {
    sample_model [i] <- rtweedie(1, xi = r$summary.hyperpar[1,1], mu = fitted_mu$mean[i], phi = r$summary.hyperpar[2,1])
  }
dm[,j] = deviance.residuals(y,sample_model) ## simulate residuals
}

2- get the empirical quantiles of the simulated residuals obtained

Dq = quantile(as.numeric(dm), (1:n - 0.5)/n)

 

3- Do the qqplot

qqplot(Dq,D)
abline(0,1)
